svg.text: Fig 7 — Dosing-disc cycle and weight check
Top: one DISPENSE k, each step in top view with a small side section. The disc rests at REST with its pocket empty. Bottom: what the load cell sees.
The turret has put column k in front. The disc is at
REST: its top is flush under column k, so the bottom
vial (#1) sits on continuous floor. Pocket is empty.
The disc swings ≈160° so the pocket is under column k;
the bottom vial (#1) drops 17 mm into it (59 ms). No
mass change yet: it is still on the weighed module.
The disc returns to REST (0.27 s) and the vial falls
through the exit hole to the fixed chute and the
shared tray. Then S2 and S1 power off.
column crossing the front position (end view)
disc top flush (0.3 mm gap): no dip, no climb
(example: column 6, midazolam, 12 g vials; HX711 at 10 samples/s; time not to scale; columns line up with frames 0–2)
still on the module, no step
vial falls through the exit hole:

g.text: 0 · pre (0.7 s), then turret move ≤ 1.8 s if needed
1 · disc → LOAD, vial drops in (wait 400 ms)

svg.text: turret move (skipped if column k is in front)
disc cycle 0.8 s (frames 1–2); S1 stays powered until REST
DISPENSE k: ≈3.2 s if the column is in front; ≤ 5 s worst
d = pre − post; u = column k’s unit mass
first, so a regular double (12 g) is not MISLOAD.
Device reports raw counts only (reply: OK col=k pre=<raw> post=<raw>); the host converts to grams, knows each
column’s drug and unit mass (regular 6 g; CS 9 / 12 / 15 g) and judges. Calibration lives on the host.
Frames and time axis not to scale. Disc start pulses: REST 600 µs, LOAD 2380 µs (≈160°, calibrated on the host). S1, S2: MG90S.
